newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed in volatile trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed in volatile trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged in mixed and volatile trading as the market remained indifferent to a reform proposal, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.04 percent, or 0.08 points, to 196.51 on an all-share turnover of 86 million shekels against 102 million on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 index gained 0.11 percent to 206.11.

"The session opened with declines of as much as 0.8 percent. Towards the end of the trading day the market recovered and started rising only to close almost unchanged. The market was unaffected by the Brodett committee and it only opened lower because of profit-taking," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
"The market is showing strength and has gained more than 14 percent in the last three weeks," Nahum said.
On Tuesday a committee led by Finance Ministry Director General David Brodett presented a proposal aimed at encouraging long-term savings and stimulating investment in the capital market.

The proposals include taxing savings of less than 10 years and reducing the amount pension funds can invest in special high-yielding government bonds. But the plan has already come under strong criticism from some groups.
"The market was expecting profit taking today, but we were all surprised by the market's strength," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir at Aharyut Investment Management.
"The market reform will not be implemented and investors showed little interest in it. The market rose very fast during the last month and a technical correction has to come soon," he said.

Africa Israel Investments, the main gainer on the Maof, rose 3.75 percent to 427,117 on volume of 4.0 million shekels. Traders said shareholders are expected to approve on Thursday the spin-off of its insurance holdings, which will enable Italian insurer Generali Spa to take control of Migdal Insurance.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries rose 3.0 percent to 139,777 on volume of 11 million shekels. On Thursday a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel is expected to announce its recommendation concerning Teva's multiple sclerosis drug Copaxone.
Bezeq Israel Telecom gained 1.50 percent to 837 on volume of 7.0 million shekels. Traders said someone was purchasing a large block of shares in Bezeq but they did not know the identity.
